acceptance_signals: The homepage main journey has no more than five substantive content sections before the footer: hero, concrete refund example, tangible report explanation, one three-step flow, and final call to action.

A first-time technically literate reader can see within the opening viewport that AgentGov keeps humans in control of AI-written code, records intended change boundaries, checks actual changes, and identifies decisions that still require a human.
The hero uses plain language, remains under 35 English words across its heading and primary support sentence, and offers one example CTA plus GitHub.
The homepage main narrative is approximately 500 English words or fewer, excluding navigation, footer, code-like report labels, and accessibility text.
Bound Verify Decide and Task Change Evidence Review are not presented as two competing repeated frameworks; only one short three-step explanation remains.

Detailed architecture, CLI transcripts, development milestones, Adapter history, version evidence, and complete PASS WARN FAIL ADVISORY teaching do not dominate the homepage and remain accessible through existing deeper links.
The refund scenario and report preview appear early and are explained in ordinary language without implying safety certification, autonomous approval, or runtime enforcement.
Existing internal links resolve, accessibility basics remain present, and the page has no unrendered templates.
At phone and desktop widths the page has no document-level horizontal overflow and retains readable hierarchy and reachable calls to action.
Relevant product-site and user-documentation tests, repository governance, task governance, scope reconciliation, and git diff validation complete with unresolved gaps reported.
README current entry, STATUS current reality, and the dated development log are updated without rewriting historical evidence.

decision.rationale: The accountable human reviewed structured proposal prp-9f69fcc4f8f1428d9252f45cd0c36026 and admitted that exact task through an explicit admission control. The local homepage now has a 31-word Hero and four main sections totaling 267 English words, with complex release and replay evidence retained through low-density links and default-collapsed disclosure. Local browser acceptance found no document overflow at phone or desktop widths. All 75 directly affected tests and the corrected complete suite of 926 tests passed with 3 platform-limited skips; task and repository governance had no FAIL, and scope rejected only excluded user-owned .codex configuration. A distinct bounded current-Agent review found no correction-required drift; because the fully specified task had no alignment journey, no native self-review completion is claimed. The task is paused locally with no commit, push, publication, release, or deployment authority, and real unbriefed-reader comprehension remains unknown.

requirement.summary: Replace the dense nine-section landing page with a substantially shorter five-part plain-language journey for technically literate first-time visitors: a concrete human-control hero, one refund example, an early tangible report surface with plain explanation, one three-step flow, and a final adoption call to action. Keep rigorous evidence and capability details available through existing deeper documentation without changing governance semantics, report content, runtime behavior, release identity, or unsupported claims.

items: Simplification could overstate runtime enforcement or imply autonomous approval.
Removing detail could disconnect claims from nearby qualification or make maturity boundaries misleading.
Tests may encode the current dense structure and need semantic updates without weakening their governance assertions.
The report preview may still expose unfamiliar status labels before the reader understands their purpose.
A word-count target could be pursued mechanically at the expense of necessary accuracy.
Unrelated user-owned .codex configuration is present and must remain untouched.
Reviewed assumption: The primary landing-page reader is technically literate but has never heard of AgentGov.
Reviewed assumption: The existing refund scenario is the strongest repository-supported concrete example.
Reviewed assumption: The existing report preview can remain visually recognizable while its surrounding explanation is simplified.
Reviewed assumption: Existing Quickstart, architecture, evidence, interview, and GitHub pages remain the appropriate deeper disclosure surfaces.
Reviewed assumption: No new visual asset is necessary for this information-architecture change.
Reviewed assumption: This task authorizes local repository edits and validation only, not commit, push, publication, release, or deployment.
Reviewed unknown: Whether the new page improves genuine unbriefed-reader comprehension remains unknown until a separate human test occurs.
Reviewed unknown: Whether a recruiter, engineering manager, and adopter respond equally well to the same simplified narrative is unknown.
Reviewed unknown: No hiring, adoption, conversion, or population-level usability improvement is established by local implementation or automated validation.
